current_answer: A U.S. software-developer posting study found roughly 14–15% fewer junior vacancies relative to senior vacancies in the year after ChatGPT’s release than in the year before. Employers also raised experience requirements within some job titles. This is a specific entry-route warning, not a count of hires or layoffs. The study compares online ads around November 2022, not firms with and without verified AI adoption; the wider tech hiring slowdown remains a rival explanation. Other research finds mixed early-career and wage patterns and no clear economy-wide U.S. AI job-loss footprint. Those outcomes cannot be collapsed into one verdict.

catalogue_card.question: Did AI shrink junior software openings?
catalogue_card.text: A U.S. study found roughly 14–15% fewer junior software ads relative to senior ads after ChatGPT. It did not count hires or isolate AI from the wider tech slowdown.

summary: A June 2026 IZA paper newly reviewed here compares U.S. software-developer postings around ChatGPT’s November 2022 release.
Junior ads requiring up to three years of experience fell roughly 14–15% relative to senior ads requiring four or more years in its main comparison.
Experience requirements rose within some job titles; remaining junior ads emphasized problem solving, communication and detail more than AI-specific skills.
The public release is a time marker. The study does not measure employer AI adoption, completed hires or layoffs.
uncertainty: The IZA study was published in June 2026 and newly reviewed here on 1 October; it does not measure a fresh October labor outcome.
The 14–15% figure is a relative junior-versus-senior vacancy estimate for U.S. software developers, not an absolute drop in junior jobs or a causal effect of AI.
freshness_note: Checked 1 October 2026. Added a June software-vacancy study; its estimate is not a new October labor outcome.
